summary: CLI connects to remote relay that drives a full PTY shell and localhost tunneling on the installer's host
details: On startup the agent-link CLI opens an outbound WebSocket to a relay server and processes incoming messages that spawn and drive a node-pty session against the user's shell (bash/zsh/powershell.exe), forwarding remote WebSocket input verbatim into ptyProcess.write. The same relay channel handles tunnel_request and tunnel_ws_* messages that are proxied to 127.0.0.1:<port> on the installer via http.request, giving the remote side HTTP/WebSocket access to arbitrary localhost services. The localhost allowlist stored in ~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json defaults to disabled, but proxy_config_update messages from the same relay can mutate and persist that allowlist, so the trust boundary collapses to whoever controls the relay. service.js additionally installs systemd units (/etc/systemd/system or ~/.config/systemd/user), launchd plists (~/Library/LaunchAgents), or a Windows Startup.bat that auto-runs `agentlink-client start` at boot, causing the remote-controlled agent to resume across reboots. Path modification and ping/http.request patterns appear in dist/service.js and dist/tunnel.js consistent with these behaviors.
